title: Assessing the probability that a positive report is false: An approach for molecular epidemiology studies
authors: S Wacholder;S Chanock;M Garcia-Closas;L El Ghormli;N Rothman
citation: Wacholder S, Chanock S, Garcia-Closas M, El ghormli L, Rothman N (2004) Assessing the probability that a positive report is false: An approach for molecular epidemiology studies. J Natl Cancer Inst 96: 434-442.
sentences: Several methodologists have pointed out [CITATION #b8][CITATION][CITATION #b10] that the high rate of nonreplication (lack of confi rmation) of research discoveries is a consequence of the convenient, yet ill-founded strategy of claiming conclusive research fi ndings solely on the basis of a single study assessed by formal statistical signifi cance, typically for a p-value less than 0.05.

As has been shown previously, the probability that a research fi nding is indeed true depends on the prior probability of it being true (before doing the study), the statistical power of the study, and the level of statistical signifi cance [CITATION][CITATION #b10].
The PPV is also the complementary probability of what Wacholder et al. have called the false positive report probability [CITATION].

Thus research fi ndings are more likely true in scientifi c fi elds with large effects, such as the impact of smoking on cancer or cardiovascular disease (relative risks [CITATION #b2][CITATION #b3][CITATION #b4][CITATION #b5][CITATION #b6][CITATION #b7][CITATION #b8][CITATION][CITATION #b10][CITATION #b11][CITATION #b12][CITATION #b13][CITATION #b14][CITATION #b15][CITATION #b16][CITATION #b17][CITATION #b18][CITATION #b19], than in scientifi c fi elds where postulated effects are small, such as genetic risk factors for multigenetic diseases (relative risks 1.1-1.5) [CITATION #b6].
Finally, instead of chasing statistical signifi cance, we should improve our understanding of the range of R values-the pre-study odds-where research efforts operate [CITATION].
